# C++ coordinate reference values

`upstream_coordinates.csv` was generated by compiling and executing
`scripts/upstream_coordinates.cpp` against the actual, unmodified upstream
`include/libgnss++/core/coordinates.hpp`. The tests do not regenerate their
expected values from the Rust implementation.

Pinned inputs:

- libgnss++: <https://github.com/rsasaki0109/gnssplusplus-library>, commit
  `72f3b7c2c4c088dc575286a6f0edf4e407bc499a` (`develop`).
- Eigen 3.4.0: <https://gitlab.com/libeigen/eigen>, commit
  `3147391d946bb4b6c68edd901f2add6ac1f31f8c`.
- Generator compiler during development: GCC 14.2.0, C++20, Linux x86_64.

To regenerate, obtain those revisions outside this checkout, then from the
project root (substitute the two source directory paths):

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_coordinates.cpp -o /tmp/upstream-coordinates
/tmp/upstream-coordinates > /tmp/upstream_coordinates.csv
diff -u tests/fixtures/upstream_coordinates.csv /tmp/upstream_coordinates.csv
```

Columns are latitude/longitude in radians, ellipsoidal height in metres,
ECEF x/y/z in metres, inverse latitude/longitude/height, ENU for the ECEF
difference `(100, -200, 300)` m, ECEF difference for ENU `(100, -200, 300)` m,
and Sagnac-corrected range to satellite ECEF `(20200000, 14000000, 21700000)` m.

The eight cases include the equator, both poles, both hemispheres, a
near-polar negative height, the documented synthetic-fixture receiver,
and GNSS satellite altitude. Tolerances are 0.1 micrometre for forward ECEF
and range, 1e-12 radians for inverse angles, 10 micrometres for inverse
height, and 1e-12 metres for ENU rotations. The inverse-height allowance
accounts for the upstream iteration's 0.1 mm stopping threshold.

This compares only core coordinate functions, not solver accuracy or full
library equivalence. Eigen and the upstream source are not vendored and
are not required to run the Rust tests. The reference outputs and generator
are distributed under the crate's MIT license with upstream attribution
retained in the root LICENSE.

## Broadcast navigation, atmosphere and SPP inputs

`scripts/upstream_navigation.cpp` calls the unmodified upstream
`navigation_internal::computeBroadcastState`, coordinate functions, and
Klobuchar/Saastamoinen model functions at the same pinned revision. It produces:

- `upstream_broadcast.nav`: five broadcast ephemerides (GPS, Galileo, QZSS,
  BeiDou GEO and BeiDou MEO).
- `upstream_navigation.csv`: 20 position/velocity/clock cases at offsets
  -300, 0, 120 and 7200 seconds. Velocity and clock drift use the same symmetric
  0.5-second finite difference as the upstream public method.
- `upstream_atmosphere.csv`: four model outputs across latitudes and elevations.
- `synthetic_spp.nav`: nine GPS ephemerides selected above 15 degrees elevation.
- `synthetic_spp.obs`: eight static, noiseless vacuum epochs, 30 seconds apart.
- `synthetic_spp_atmosphere.obs`: the same receiver and satellites with the
  upstream default Klobuchar and Saastamoinen delays applied.

The receiver truth is 35 degrees N, 139 degrees E, 45 m WGS-84 ellipsoidal
height, with receiver clock bias 2 microseconds. Epochs start at GPS week
2300, tow 345600. The approximate header position is deliberately offset
(+100, -50, +30) m. The generator iterates the code transmit-time equation,
including satellite-clock transmit-time adjustment, relativistic clock,
Sagnac range and TGD. Measurements are rounded to 0.001 m or cycles.
L1/L2 phases carry fixed integer ambiguities and, where enabled,
opposite-sign dispersive ionosphere delays. They are retained to exercise
the parser; they do not validate an RTK/PPP solver, wind-up, cycle-slip
recovery, or real-data accuracy.

From the project root, with the pinned upstream and Eigen sources available:

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_navigation.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/types.cpp \
  -o /tmp/upstream-navigation
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-navigation-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-navigation /tmp/upstream-navigation-fixtures
```

Compare the generated files with the checked-in files before updating them.
Broadcast comparison tolerances are 0.1 mm position, 1e-6 m/s velocity,
and 1e-15 seconds/seconds-per-second clock bias/drift, including rounding
introduced by the RINEX navigation text. Atmospheric tolerances are 1e-9 m
for ionosphere and 1e-8 m for troposphere. SPP truth bounds are 3 mm per ECEF
component, 1e-11 s clock bias and <1 mm residual RMS.
These are component and synthetic tests; no upstream SPP/RTK/PPP solver
output or runtime is compared by this generator.

## LAMBDA reference candidates

`upstream_lambda.csv` is generated by `scripts/upstream_lambda.cpp`, calling
the unmodified pinned `src/algorithms/lambda.cpp` and Eigen version above.
It contains 11 cases and 34 candidates: negative half-integers, exact integers,
one requested candidate, positive/negative correlation, near-singular covariance,
three-dimensional decorrelation, ties, and dense 4/8/12-dimensional cases.
Each row stores the input, candidate index and integer vector, squared ILS
residual, reduced D/Z/z/Qz diagnostics and second/best ratio. Matrices in the CSV
are row-major. The format header specifies the variable-length column groups.

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_lambda.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/algorithms/lambda.cpp \
  -o /tmp/upstream-lambda
/tmp/upstream-lambda > /tmp/upstream_lambda.csv
diff -u tests/fixtures/upstream_lambda.csv /tmp/upstream_lambda.csv
```

Candidate integers and Z must match exactly. The C++ LU back-transform returns
floating-point values, so its candidate components are checked within 1e-8 of
integers before comparing their integer values. D/z/Qz, residuals and ratios
use 1e-12 times max(1, abs(reference)) tolerance.
Tests also compare 100 seeded two-dimensional positive-definite correlated
cases against independent exhaustive lattice enumeration with an analytic
inverse covariance. These validate integer least-squares components, not FIX
reliability, partial AR, an RTK/PPP solution, or runtime parity.

LAMBDA is RTKLIB-derived; keep the original attribution and redistribution
conditions in `LICENSE-RTKLIB` with this source and generated reference.

## RTK FLOAT components and static base/rover inputs

`scripts/upstream_rtk_float.cpp` executes the pinned, unmodified
`kalman.hpp` (with every state force-active) and `rtk_measurement.cpp`.
`upstream_rtk_update.csv` has three cases: a dense correlated update containing
zero states, shared-reference phase/code DD blocks, and precise phase rows.
Rows record prior state/covariance, H, innovations, R, posterior state/covariance,
NIS, innovation variances, and the DD ambiguity and head cross-covariance
transform. Matrices are row-major; the CSV header describes the column groups.
State/covariance/NIS/transform tolerances are 1e-10 times max(1, abs(reference));
innovation variances use 1e-12. Rust uses Cholesky, Joseph covariance update and
explicit activation of zero states; the native comparison uses upstream LU and
(I-KH)P. This compares linear components, not the full upstream RTKProcessor.

The generator reuses the navigation fixture helpers and calls the upstream
unmodified broadcast, geodist, ENU and Saastamoinen functions. It generates:

- `synthetic_rtk.nav`: nine GPS satellites visible above 15 degrees.
- `synthetic_rtk_base.obs` / `synthetic_rtk_rover.obs`: 32 static code/phase pairs.
- `synthetic_rtk_base_noisy.obs` / `synthetic_rtk_rover_noisy.obs`: those pairs
  with deterministic sinusoidal code noise of amplitude 0.05 m and phase noise
  of amplitude 0.0005 m, differing between receivers and satellites.
- `synthetic_rtk_truth.csv`: base ECEF, rover ECEF, initial rover seed, and the
  satellite's SD ambiguities in cycles, with distinct DD integers.

Base truth is WGS-84 35 degrees N, 139 degrees E, 45 m height. Rover ENU offset
is (12, -7, 3) m, a sqrt(202) = 14.21 m baseline. The initial rover seed has ECEF
error (+1, -0.5, +0.3) m. Receiver clocks are -1 microsecond base and +2
microseconds rover. Epochs start at GPS week 2300, tow 345600 and are 30 s apart.
The iterative transmit-time equation includes satellite clock, Sagnac, TGD and
Saastamoinen. No ionosphere, antenna effects, wind-up, moving receiver or real
noise is simulated. Code is rounded to 1e-5 m and phase to 1e-4 cycles to fit
RINEX's 14-character value fields.

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_rtk_float.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/types.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/algorithms/rtk_measurement.cpp \
  -o /tmp/upstream-rtk-float
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-rtk-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-rtk-float /tmp/upstream-rtk-fixtures
```

Compare all seven generated files with the checked-in fixtures before updates.
Tests require every epoch to be FLOAT, 3-D error <3 mm for the noiseless pairs,
and <15 cm for the noisy pairs. Noiseless best integer candidates must match the
known DD integers; their ratio never promotes the result to FIX. Additional
mutated inputs test reference changes, slips with LLI, half-cycles, satellite
loss/reappearance, power failure, long gaps, innovation rejection, malformed
inputs, time ordering and failed-update continuity. The initial FIX tests below
use the same inputs; full RTKProcessor FIX policies, real-data accuracy and
runtime/memory parity remain unverified.

## Initial RTK integer conditioning and FIX validation

`scripts/upstream_rtk_fix.cpp` calls the pinned, unmodified native
`rtk_ar_evaluation::solveFixedHeadState` and `rtk_cp_pr_gate::evaluate` functions.
`upstream_rtk_fix.csv` contains five joint Gaussian cases: ordinary conditioning,
zero head/exact integers, small conditional variance, strong cross-correlation,
and a different head/ambiguity dimension. Native fixed means and Eigen LDLT
quadratic costs are recorded. Upstream exposes no conditional-covariance API:
the covariance reference is an independent Eigen Schur complement, not an
upstream FIX covariance output. Rust uses the joint Cholesky conditional block
to avoid subtraction cancellation. Mean/covariance/cost tolerances are
1e-11 times max(1, abs(reference)).

`upstream_rtk_code_phase.csv` contains three native position-independent
`DD_PR - (DD_CP - fixed ambiguity metres)` gate cases, including equality at
the 0.5 m boundary and one invalid pair. Consistency/bad-pair counts match
exactly; RMS/max use 1e-14 times max(1, abs(reference)). Rust additionally rejects
any nonfinite pair instead of dropping it.

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_rtk_fix.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/types.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/algorithms/rtk_measurement.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/algorithms/rtk_ar_evaluation.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/algorithms/rtk_cp_pr_gate.cpp \
  -o /tmp/upstream-rtk-fix
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-rtk-fix-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-rtk-fix /tmp/upstream-rtk-fix-fixtures
diff -u tests/fixtures/upstream_rtk_fix.csv /tmp/upstream-rtk-fix-fixtures/upstream_rtk_fix.csv
diff -u tests/fixtures/upstream_rtk_code_phase.csv /tmp/upstream-rtk-fix-fixtures/upstream_rtk_code_phase.csv
```

The initial Rust `rtk` policy uses full-set AR, five-epoch lock, ratio >=3,
two consecutive confirmations, covariance, actual phase/code residuals,
code/phase consistency, postfit NIS and static history checks. README records
the thresholds. They are an initial conservative policy, not a reproduction
of all upstream RTKProcessor options (including PAR, FFRT and fix-and-hold).
The same noisy/noiseless inputs produce five FLOAT then 27 FIX epochs, with
every FIX integer equal to the known truth. Maximum 3-D FIX errors are
0.000031943 m noiseless and 0.000861191 m noisy. Regression bounds are <3 mm
and <5 mm respectively. These synthetic results do not establish real-data
accuracy or false-fix rates.

Tests inject wrong integers, persistent fractional phase bias, a transient
phase outlier with high ratio, a strict static-history gate, LLI slip, reference
loss/reacquisition, power failure, gaps, explicit events and failed updates.
Each rejection preserves the numerical FLOAT estimator, clears pending
confirmation, and emits no FIX. Arc resets require fresh lock and confirmation.
Duplicate evaluation cannot inflate confirmation. CLI tests check all 32
statuses, rejection/confirmation reasons and candidate diagnostic columns.

## SP3 / RINEX CLK and precise interpolation

`scripts/upstream_precise.cpp` generates complete SP3-d P and RINEX CLK 3.00 AS
files and runs the pinned, unmodified `src/core/precise_products.cpp` and
`preciseClockRelativisticCorrection`. Inputs are polynomial moving tracks,
not measurements or actual GNSS orbits: G01 and E12 have 12 orbit epochs at
300 s spacing, plus a two-epoch SP3; G01 has 40 CLK epochs at 90 s spacing.
Start is GPS week 2300, tow 345600 (2024-02-08 00:00:00 GPST).
The SP3 header declares IGS20, accuracy bases/exponents and antenna phase centre.
Clock datums deliberately differ: G01 SP3 is about 20 microseconds and CLK
about 50 microseconds; E12 SP3 clock is exactly zero and has no CLK rows.
Orbit components are rounded to 1 mm and SP3 clocks to 1 ps by their fields.

`upstream_precise.csv` has 64 satellite queries (GPS and Galileo, both ends,
interior, exact samples, fractional times, dense and two-point interpolation).
All 64 compare position/velocity/periodic relativity. Clock comparisons use:

- Mode 0: SP3-only native interpolation (18 cases).
- Mode 1: native interpolation on the CLK-only G01 grid; before loading CLK,
  the generator explicitly clears G01 SP3 clock-valid flags in native input
  records. E12 keeps its SP3 clocks (18 cases).
- Mode 2: the two-point SP3 (10 cases).
- Mode 3: unmodified native SP3+CLK loading/merging (18 cases). E12 matches
  unchanged SP3 (9 cases). G01's nine mixed-grid outputs expose a deliberate
  policy difference; Rust keeps the satellite on the CLK grid throughout.
  The test requires a clock-bias difference >1e-7 s on at least one mixed query.

Thus 55 clock/drift cases compare identical admitted sample grids; the other
nine are policy-difference records, not clock-parity passes. Native source is
unchanged; mode 1 adapts the input validity flags explicitly. Matrix/solver
code from Rust never generates these reference values.

Absolute tolerances: position 1e-6 m, velocity 2e-7 m/s, bias/relativity 1e-16 s,
drift 1e-16 s/s. Both implementations use a centred/clamped window of up to ten
samples, Neville polynomial interpolation and a +/-1 s central derivative.
Rust additionally requires at least two samples, rejects extrapolation by
default, rejects gaps >900 s and splits SP3 arcs at missing/quality boundaries.
It preserves CLK sigma/drift/rate fields, but query drift is calculated from
the bias interpolant, matching the native interpolation component.

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_precise.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/types.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/precise_products.cpp \
  -o /tmp/upstream-precise
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-precise-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-precise /tmp/upstream-precise-fixtures
for name in synthetic_precise.sp3 synthetic_precise_two.sp3 synthetic_precise.clk upstream_precise.csv; do
  diff -u "tests/fixtures/$name" "/tmp/upstream-precise-fixtures/$name"
done
```

Boundary tests also mutate headers/epochs/records to check satellite declaration
continuations in SP3-c/d, GPS week crossing, fractional queries, UTC/BDT/GAL/QZS
conversion, unknown time systems, SP3 missing/zero clocks, predicted data,
manoeuvres/clock events, CLK-only source selection through a gap, explicit
bounded extrapolation, RINEX 3.04 headers, Fortran exponents and six-value
continuations. Invalid/truncated/duplicate/out-of-order/unsupported records
are errors. The first midpoint query is independently executable using
`cargo run --release --locked --offline --example precise --
tests/fixtures/synthetic_precise.sp3 tests/fixtures/synthetic_precise.clk`.
These are product-component regressions; PPP receiver solutions, real-product
accuracy, upstream whole-processor compatibility and runtime parity remain
unverified.

## Precise transmission time and initial code SPP

`scripts/upstream_precise_transmit.cpp` uses the same pinned libgnss++ source,
GCC 14.2.0 and Eigen 3.4.0. It first regenerates the four interpolation fixtures
above. It then calls native interpolation, periodic relativity, geometric range
and atmosphere components. Reception-time Taylor projection follows the formulas
in upstream `src/algorithms/spp.cpp` and `ppp_corrections.cpp`: subtract velocity
times flight time from reception position, subtract clock drift times flight
time from the published clock, and add periodic relativity once. The alternative
emission-time interpolation is an independent iteration in this C++ generator.
Neither path executes the complete upstream SPPProcessor or PPPProcessor.

`upstream_precise_transmit.csv` contains 80 cases: two clock grids, two methods,
G01/E12, five reception times and two receiver positions. The clock grids are
SP3-only and CLK-only for G01 (with its SP3 clock-valid flags explicitly cleared
in the native input, as in interpolation mode 1 above). E12 retains SP3 clocks.
The file records receiver coordinates, reception/emission GPS times, flight
time, iteration count, satellite position/velocity, published clock/drift,
periodic relativity, total clock and Earth-rotation-corrected geometric range.
Rust compares emission tow to 1e-10 s, flight time to 1e-13 s, position/range
to 1e-6 m, velocity to 2e-7 m/s, and clock/drift/relativity to 1e-16 in their
respective SI units; iteration counts match exactly.

The separate `synthetic_precise_spp.*` products cover nine GPS satellites:
12 SP3 orbit epochs at 300 s spacing and 40 CLK epochs at 90 s spacing.
Orbit positions are generated by native broadcast-orbit components and stored
at 1 mm resolution. The SP3 declares IGS20 and APC for this synthetic model;
its clocks are all missing, so native loading cannot mix the SP3 and CLK grids.
The CLK contains independently defined polynomial clocks, without periodic
relativity or broadcast TGD. These are synthetic products, not IGS observations.

The Taylor and emission RINEX observation files each have eight epochs spaced
30 s apart, starting at GPS week 2300, tow 346200. Each has nine C1C measurements
generated from native geometry, precise clock plus periodic relativity,
Saastamoinen delay, a 2 microsecond receiver clock and a known per-satellite
code delay, rounded to 1e-5 m. There is no ionosphere, measurement noise, carrier
phase, antenna offset, tide or receiver motion. The truth file contains receiver
coordinates, an offset acquisition seed and receiver clock.

The bias CSV is a demo ledger, not Bias-SINEX or a DCB/OSB parser. Its nine rows
declare additive corrections (`corrected P = raw P + correction_m`) for each
satellite's `1C` tracking code, RinexClk source, caller-declared clock reference
`synthetic-precise-clock-v1`, and inclusive reception-time validity from GPS
week 2300, tow 346200 through 346410. The reference name does not independently
identify or authenticate a product clock datum. A declared zero correction is
accepted; omitted, expired or mismatched corrections are rejected.

The Rust end-to-end regressions recover all eight SPP positions and clocks for
both input methods: maximum 3-D errors are 0.000010654 m (Taylor) and
0.000009824 m (emission), with regression limits of 1 mm, 1e-12 s receiver-clock
error and 1e-4 m residual RMS. Release examples also produce eight nine-satellite
SPP rows and satisfy these bounds. These noiseless synthetic checks establish
neither phase PPP, real-product accuracy nor full upstream solver parity.
Boundary tests exercise transmission coverage, manoeuvres/clock events, missing
CLK without SP3 fallback, week crossing, nonconvergence, code-bias validity and
source/reference mismatches, coordinate/reference-point declarations, receiver
clock offsets and seedless acquisition.

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_precise_transmit.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/types.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/precise_products.cpp \
  -o /tmp/upstream-precise-transmit
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-precise-transmit-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-precise-transmit /tmp/upstream-precise-transmit-fixtures
for name in synthetic_precise.sp3 synthetic_precise_two.sp3 synthetic_precise.clk upstream_precise.csv upstream_precise_transmit.csv synthetic_precise_spp.sp3 synthetic_precise_spp.clk synthetic_precise_spp_bias.csv synthetic_precise_spp_truth.csv synthetic_precise_spp_taylor.obs synthetic_precise_spp_emission.obs; do
  diff -u "tests/fixtures/$name" "/tmp/upstream-precise-transmit-fixtures/$name"
done
```

## Initial dual-frequency code/phase observations

`scripts/upstream_dual_frequency.cpp` links the unmodified pinned
`src/algorithms/ppp.cpp` using function/data sections and linker garbage
collection, retaining the actual `ppp_utils::getIonosphereFreeCoefficients`
and `calculateMelbourneWubbena` functions. It uses native physical constants
and the IF code/phase and independent-noise variance expressions from
`ppp_observations.cpp`. GF is the native state-path expression
`lambda1 * L1 - lambda2 * L2`. These expressions are evaluated in an independent
C++ generator, not the Rust implementation. Neither the upstream full observation
selection policy nor PPPProcessor is executed. Degenerate frequency pairs are
rejected by Rust, whereas the native coefficient utility returns `(1, 0)`.

`upstream_dual_frequency.csv` has 48 cases across 12 ordered signal pairs:
GPS L1/L2, L1/L5, L2/L5; QZSS L1/L2, L1/L5; Galileo E1/E5a, E1/E5b;
BeiDou B1I/B2I, B1I/B3I, B1C/B2a; GLONASS FDMA L1/L2 at channels -7 and +6.
Every pair has four test points with geometric common terms
`23000000.125 + 17.5*i` m, first-frequency ionosphere `4.25*i` m and
second-frequency ionosphere scaled by `f1²/f2²`. Code has positive ionosphere;
phase in metres has negative ionosphere and integer-cycle offsets
`N1 = 12+i`, `N2 = -7+2*i`. The generator records raw codes, cycle phases,
frequencies, native coefficients, IF code/phase, GF/MW, nominal independent-noise
variances (0.25 m² code and 0.0001 m² phase per frequency), and the resulting
real-valued IF ambiguity `a*lambda1*N1 + b*lambda2*N2` in metres.

The nominal variances are measurement weights; no random noise is added.
The changing offsets are separate component test points, not a continuous
slip-free phase arc or a full satellite/receiver solution. There are no precise
products, physical orbit geometry, atmosphere, antennas, OSBs or wind-up here.
For native-reference comparison Rust declares additive zero code/phase
corrections and synthetic clock/phase datum names explicitly.

Absolute tolerances for CSV comparison: frequencies exact, coefficients 1e-14,
IF code/phase and GF/MW 1e-7 m, code variance 1e-12 m² and phase variance 1e-14 m².
Dispersive first-order ionosphere cancellation and the residual metre ambiguity
are checked independently to 1e-6 m. The generic MW formula compares all pairs,
but the observation builder excludes GLONASS MW diagnostics like the ordinary
upstream PPP state path; it retains GLONASS GF and FDMA channel provenance.

`synthetic_dual_frequency.obs` represents the same 12 satellites at four
GPS epochs starting at week 2300, tow 345600 with 30 s spacing. It declares
per-system tracking codes, GLONASS slots/channels, and observation continuation
lines. Codes are rounded to 1e-5 m, phase to 1e-4 cycles, with raw LLI 0 and
signal-strength indicator 7. Reading the file and forming the selected IF pairs
produces all 48 measurements. Quantisation-aware bounds are 1 mm for IF/MW and
0.1 mm for GF; these are input-rounding bounds, not relaxed CSV tolerances.

Other tests verify nonzero additive corrections before combination while raw
GF/MW remain unchanged, frequency-correlated noise, explicit tracking selection,
missing/duplicate observations, code/phase correction provenance and validity,
half-cycle exclusion, either signal's LLI reset request, power failure,
unsupported signals, degenerate pairs, invalid FDMA channels, invalid epochs,
full-week validity and nonfinite inputs. The builder is stateless; phase arc
continuity, GF/MW slip thresholds, ambiguity estimation and PPP accuracy remain
unimplemented/unverified. The release example inspects G01's four pairs only.

```bash
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_dual_frequency.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/algorithms/ppp.cpp \
  -Wl,--gc-sections -o /tmp/upstream-dual-frequency
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-dual-frequency-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-dual-frequency \
  /tmp/upstream-dual-frequency-fixtures/upstream_dual_frequency.csv \
  /tmp/upstream-dual-frequency-fixtures/synthetic_dual_frequency.obs
diff -u tests/fixtures/upstream_dual_frequency.csv /tmp/upstream-dual-frequency-fixtures/upstream_dual_frequency.csv
diff -u tests/fixtures/synthetic_dual_frequency.obs /tmp/upstream-dual-frequency-fixtures/synthetic_dual_frequency.obs
```

## Initial phase-arc continuity and slip predicates

`scripts/upstream_phase_arc.cpp` includes the pinned, unmodified
`src/algorithms/ppp_internal.hpp` and calls the actual
`geometryFreeSlipThresholdMeters(false, configured)` helper. The MW threshold
`max(10, configured * 100)` and strict absolute-difference comparisons are
literal expressions from the ordinary IF path in `ppp_state.cpp`. There is
no standalone native MW-slip predicate API. This independent generator evaluates
those expressions; it does not run `PPPProcessor::detectCycleSlips`, native
observation selection, ambiguity-state management, CLAS or MADOCA policies.

`upstream_phase_arc.csv` contains 48 predicate cases: four configured thresholds
(0.05, 0.2, 0.5 and 0.75 m), with zero differences, positive/negative threshold
equality, the adjacent representable values above magnitude equality,
simultaneous GF/MW jumps, and missing previous/current MW. The GF effective
floor is 0.5 m; MW has a 10 m floor with the configured threshold times 100.
Rust compares effective thresholds and boolean decisions exactly. Missing MW
cannot vote; nonfinite diagnostics/configuration are rejected in separate tests.
These checks establish predicate agreement, not full native slip-policy parity.

`synthetic_phase_arc.obs` is an independently generated GPS C1C/L1C/C2W/L2W
RINEX 3.04 input for G01/G02, starting at GPS week 2300, tow 345600.
The common metre term is `23000000.125 + satellite_number*1000 + 5*seconds`;
L1 ionosphere is `0.001*seconds` m and L2 scales by `f1²/f2²`. Raw code has
positive ionosphere; cycle phase has negative ionosphere and integer offsets.
Initial integers are N1=12 and N2=-7. Native frequency/light-speed constants are
used; there are no orbit products, calibrated physical geometry, antennas,
noise, wind-up, tides or position estimation. Code rounds to 1e-5 m, phase to
1e-4 cycles. Raw LLI and strength are written explicitly.

The 16 input epochs have these deliberately injected events (zero-based index):

| Epoch | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 0–1 | Both satellites start and continue constant-integer arcs |
| 2 | G01 L1 adds four cycles with loss-of-lock LLI |
| 3 | New integer arc continues |
| 4 | G01 L2 phase missing; both codes remain present |
| 5 | G01 phase reappears |
| 6 | G01 L1 adds five cycles without LLI; GF jump exceeds 0.5 m |
| 7 | Test/example rejects G01's otherwise eligible phase update; G02 is accepted |
| 8 | G01 entirely absent |
| 9 | G01 reappears |
| 10 | Receiver power-failure flag 1 |
| 11 | G01 L2 half-cycle LLI |
| 12 | Sparse flag 6 event contains only G01; tracker interrupts both satellites |
| 13 | Both resume after event |
| 14 | A 180 s gap instead of 30 s; both restart |
| 15 | G01 L1 code adds 25 m; MW jumps, GF remains below threshold |

The epoch 15 MW jump is a code anomaly, not a true carrier-cycle slip; this
distinction is intentional. Detection returns discontinuity candidates and
conservatively restarts the arc, without claiming the reason proves a slip.
All other ordinary gaps are 30 s. The epoch 7 rejection is supplied externally
by the Rust test/example, not encoded as a RINEX receiver event.

The complete reader/model/tracker trace records 26 accepted phases and 13
accepted arc IDs, retains code-only measurements at phase outages, and keeps
G02's arc across G01's rejection. It does not estimate ambiguity values or PPP
positions. Independent tests check prepare/finish separation, no premature
history or lock increments, invalid acceptance retry, empty-set failure,
rejected-ID nonreuse, signal/FDMA channel and datum/correction changes,
unchanged-datum validity extension, noise changes, full-week/time ordering,
strict gap equality, invalid forward input and explicit external invalidation.
The initial Rust continuity policy resets on any additive correction-value
change and treats flag 6 as receiver-wide interruption; these conservative
choices are not a claim of whole-processor lifecycle parity. Smooth dynamic
corrections and SSR discontinuity counters remain future work.

Reproduction (GCC 14.2.0, Eigen 3.4.0, pinned source above, Linux x86_64):

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O1 \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/algorithms -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_phase_arc.cpp -o /tmp/upstream-phase-arc
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-phase-arc-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-phase-arc \
  /tmp/upstream-phase-arc-fixtures/upstream_phase_arc.csv \
  /tmp/upstream-phase-arc-fixtures/synthetic_phase_arc.obs
diff -u tests/fixtures/upstream_phase_arc.csv /tmp/upstream-phase-arc-fixtures/upstream_phase_arc.csv
diff -u tests/fixtures/synthetic_phase_arc.obs /tmp/upstream-phase-arc-fixtures/synthetic_phase_arc.obs
```

# Initial static GPS IF PPP references

`scripts/upstream_ppp.cpp` produces nine files using the pinned native source
and Eigen revisions above. It reuses the precise-transmit generator's orbit,
clock and product helpers through a renamed entry point; native source is
unchanged. Rebuilding the original precise-transmit generator after this entry
point change reproduced all eleven existing product/transmit/SPP files exactly.
This generator does **not** execute `PPPProcessor` or its state, admission,
initialization, covariance, convergence or slip policies.

- `upstream_niell.csv`: 96 calls to native `niellHydrostaticMapping` from
  `include/libgnss++/models/troposphere.hpp`. Eight latitudes from −90° to 90°
  include southern/northern seasons and latitude interpolation/clamping.
  Heights cycle through −100, 45 and 2000 m; each latitude uses elevations
  0°, 5° and 90° and day numbers 1, 39, 200 and 366. Rust matches within
  1e-12. Independent calendar checks include leap centuries and year rollover.
- `upstream_ppp_model.csv`: 54 geometry, clock, NMF and IF code predictions:
  nine satellites, three epochs (indices 0, 31, 63), true and offset receivers.
  Native precise interpolation, periodic relativity, geodist and coordinates
  are used with the literal ordinary PPP expression
  `rho + clock_m - c*sat_clock + NMF*zenith_m`. The five design columns add
  first-order Sagnac position derivatives to −LOS; this is an explicit Rust
  model choice, different from native ordinary PPP's −LOS-only row. Mapping
  and satellite receiver-position derivatives are neglected. Tolerances:
  range/prediction 1e-6 m, clock 1e-16 s, elevation 1e-11 rad, NMF/design 1e-10.
- `upstream_ppp_admission.csv`: 576 independently evaluated elevations at the
  true receiver, one for every epoch/satellite, with a 10° mask. Both Rust
  traces match every admitted satellite set: nine for epochs 0–55, eight for
  epochs 56–63 (G09 falls below the mask), 568 code and 568 phase admissions.

`synthetic_ppp.sp3` and `.clk` reuse the existing twelve-point, 300 s orbit and
forty-point, 90 s clock products. They declare synthetic IGS20/APC; all SP3
clocks are missing, so the native comparison never mixes CLK and SP3 clocks.
Synthetic antenna offsets are zero. The two RINEX 3.04 files each contain 64
epochs at 30 s spacing, GPS week 2300, tow 346200 through 348090, with nine
GPS satellites and C1C/L1C/C2W/L2W. Raw LLI is zero and strength is seven.

The true receiver is WGS-84 35° N, 139° E, 45 m. Its initial seed is offset
by (5, −3, 2) m and is rounded to 1e-4 m in the observation header. The true
receiver clock is `2e-6 + epoch_index*5e-10` s, independent initial clock zero,
and zenith total delay 2.4 m mapped with native Niell at day 39; initial filter
zenith delay is 2.3 m. There is no separate dry/wet atmosphere or gradient.
L1 ionosphere is `4 + 0.01*PRN + 0.002*(tow-346200)` m and L2 scales by
f1²/f2²; code adds it and phase subtracts it. Native constants and IF equations
form N1=`12+PRN`, N2=`-7+2*PRN`. True coordinates, seed and meter IF
ambiguities are stored in `synthetic_ppp_truth.csv`.

Nonzero frequency-specific code and phase offsets are added to raw data.
`synthetic_ppp_bias.csv` stores their **negative**, additive corrections in
18 rows, with tracking code, CLK source, named clock and phase references,
and an inclusive GPS reception-time validity interval covering all epochs.
This is a synthetic ledger, not a Bias-SINEX/DCB/OSB parser. TGD, antenna,
wind-up, tides and extra ionosphere models are not applied.

`synthetic_ppp_noisy.obs` additionally uses deterministic code noise
`0.05*sin(0.37*i+0.53*PRN+j)` m and phase noise
`0.001*sin(0.29*i+0.31*PRN+j)` m, where i is epoch index and j frequency index
0 or 1. These are correlated sinusoidal perturbations, not stochastic or real
receiver noise. Both files round code to 1e-5 m and phase to 1e-4 cycles.
The Rust configured per-frequency variances are 0.0025 m² code and 1e-6 m²
phase, without frequency cross covariance in this fixture; separate component
tests check correlated frequency propagation. Code/phase cross noise and
satellite cross noise are assumed independent by this initial PPP filter.

All 64 epochs in each trace produce PPP FLOAT, never FIX. Synthetic regression
bounds: noiseless maximum position error <2 mm and final position, clock in
meters, zenith and ambiguity error <1 mm; noisy maximum position error <1 m
and each final error <1 cm. Final code/phase RMS bounds are 0.1/0.1 mm
noiseless and 0.2/0.005 m noisy. These are truth-based regression bounds,
not native whole-filter covariance or solution tolerances or real accuracy.
Tests also check an initial carrier gauge shifted by −20,000,000 m,
single-update covariance without double-counting iterative measurements,
numerical state preservation after innovation/postfit rejection, slips,
phase outages, events, missing selected CLK without SP3 fallback, clock-source
or frame mismatch, singular geometry, nonconvergence and input ordering.
The absence of complete native PPP output, real datasets and matched runtime
measurements remains a gap in the final parity goal.

Reproduction (GCC 14.2.0, pinned source and Eigen above, Linux x86_64):

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_ppp.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/types.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/precise_products.cpp \
  -o /tmp/upstream-ppp
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-ppp-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-ppp /tmp/upstream-ppp-fixtures
for file in synthetic_ppp.sp3 synthetic_ppp.clk synthetic_ppp.obs \
  synthetic_ppp_noisy.obs synthetic_ppp_truth.csv synthetic_ppp_bias.csv \
  upstream_niell.csv upstream_ppp_model.csv upstream_ppp_admission.csv; do
  cmp "tests/fixtures/$file" "/tmp/upstream-ppp-fixtures/$file" || exit 1
done
```

# Initial Bias-SINEX satellite OSB references

`scripts/upstream_bias.cpp` links the pinned, **unmodified** native
`src/core/ionex_dcb_products.cpp` and `types.cpp`. It calls `DCBProducts::loadFile`
and `getBias`; unit conversion is the literal anonymous-namespace function
from `ppp_corrections.cpp`, while the measurement subtraction sign is the native
`ppp_correction_contract::measurementCorrectionSign(false, false)` call.
It does not execute PPPProcessor, native phase OSB application or DSB-to-OSB
datum resolution. Only ns/metre conversion is compared with native; phase cyc
conversion is a Rust extension with independent analytic tests.

The generator writes three files:

- `synthetic_ppp_osb.bsx`: 36 OSB rows, the same nine satellites and two code
  plus two phase observables as the previous PPP fixtures. Values are the
  **positive raw injected biases**, whose negatives reproduce the prior
  additive correction ledger. L1 biases use ns and L2 biases use m. All have
  SVN/PRN, blank STATION and OBS2, GPS TIME_SYSTEM and ABSOLUTE BIAS_MODE.
  The half-open validity is 2024:039:00600 through 2024:039:02520, covering
  the existing 64 reception epochs. Code sigma is 0.001 and phase sigma
  0.00001 in the row's native unit; these are retained as product provenance,
  not automatically treated as fresh independent measurement errors.
- `upstream_bias.bsx`: the same 36 OSBs with repeated OBS1 in OBS2, plus
  a Galileo DSB, open-ended BeiDou metre OSB and QZSS OSB in scientific
  notation (39 total). Native whitespace parsing requires OBS2 even for
  OSB and drops standard blank-OBS2 rows; the separate files expose this
  difference instead of pretending native accepts both. Native also ignores
  validity, description metadata and end-marker completeness. Rust admits
  only valid, explicitly timed/bound rows and rejects incomplete files.
- `upstream_bias.csv`: all 39 native-loaded rows and native `getBias` results,
  original units/value/sigma, literal metre conversion and native code
  additive sign. Rust matches raw values/sigma exactly and conversion/sign
  within absolute 2e-15 m. DSB output is a component conversion reference,
  not permission to apply DSB as an absolute correction.

Rust tests additionally cover OSB blank/duplicate second columns, retained
station rows that cannot supply satellite corrections, missing/expired code,
missing/expired/unbound phase, adjacent half-open periods, overlapping and
open intervals, declared/conflicting/missing time scale, GPS/UTC/BDT conversion,
leap centuries and the UTC leap-second boundary, exact tracking identities,
GLONASS FDMA cycle-unit channel requirements, duplicate requests, malformed
rows, unsupported slopes/units/versions, I/O failures and invalid bindings.
Repeated satellite-clock-reference description rows remain separate; they
do not automatically certify compatibility with the precise clocks.

The PPP integration reads the standard blank-OBS2 file and checks both entire
64-epoch traces against the existing additive ledger: state mean/covariance
within absolute 1e-7 m/m², identical status, admission and arc lifecycle.
Per-epoch correction snapshots have exact-epoch inclusive ledger validity,
so original product half-open boundaries cannot accidentally become inclusive.
Updating that validity alone preserves arcs. A separate adjacent-period test
changes only G01 L1 phase bias by +0.02 m at epoch 8 and verifies its ambiguity
restarts with the expected −a*0.02 m change, while all other arcs continue.
Other integration cases cover a missing L2 phase OSB retaining code, phase
reacquisition, inconsistent clock datum and explicit external arc invalidation
when code correction preparation fails before calling the filter.
These are synthetic/component checks, not real Bias-SINEX accuracy or whole
native PPPProcessor state/phase/initialization/runtime parity.

Reproduction (GCC 14.2.0, pinned source and Eigen above, Linux x86_64):

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_bias.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/types.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/ionex_dcb_products.cpp \
  -o /tmp/upstream-bias
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-bias-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-bias /tmp/upstream-bias-fixtures
for file in synthetic_ppp_osb.bsx upstream_bias.bsx upstream_bias.csv; do
  cmp "tests/fixtures/$file" "/tmp/upstream-bias-fixtures/$file" || exit 1
done
```

# Initial nominal-yaw phase wind-up references

`scripts/upstream_windup.cpp` links the **unmodified** pinned `ppp.cpp` and
calls `ppp_utils::calculatePhaseWindup`. `scripts/upstream_windup_sun.cpp`
includes the **actual** pinned `ppp_corrections.cpp` (found through its source
directory include path) and exposes its anonymous-namespace
`approximateSunPositionEcef` through a small wrapper. Function/data sections
and linker garbage collection keep unused whole-processor paths out of the
executable. No native source is patched, extracted into a rewritten formula,
or replaced with a Rust-generated expectation. The precise-transmit helper
reuses the independent native product/orbit machinery described above.

Five generated files:

- `upstream_windup_sun.csv`: twelve actual native solar positions, GPS weeks
  0, 1042, 2300, 2301 at tow 0, 346200.25 and 604799.75. Tests compare each
  ECEF component within 1e-3 m at solar distances near 1.5e11 m. Native JD
  uses fractional GPS labels directly, without a GPS→UTC, UT1/EOP, nutation
  or polar-motion conversion; this is a low-order Sun model, not astronomy
  ephemeris accuracy or a claim of those corrections being negligible.
- `upstream_windup.csv`: 360 direct native nominal-yaw calls: the twelve
  solar positions, receiver latitudes −70/−35/0/35/70° at 139° E and height
  45 m, two native synthetic broadcast satellite positions, previous cycles
  −2.25/0/3.75. Some geometry is below the horizon; these are dipole-formula
  component cases, not usable PPP observations. Comparison is absolute
  2e-12 cycle. Separate analytic tests rotate explicit frames through three
  turns in both directions and check principal branch crossings, native
  round-away-from-zero ties and degenerate frames, LOS and Sun directions.
- `upstream_ppp_windup.csv`: all nine satellites × 64 existing PPP epochs
  (576 rows), using the true receiver and native receive-time Taylor transmit
  positions, actual solar helper, prior and new wind-up cycles, and negative
  IF correction `-cycles*c/(f1+f2)`. These are component/correction references,
  not output from running the complete native PPPProcessor.
- `synthetic_ppp_windup.obs` and `synthetic_ppp_windup_noisy.obs`: each starts
  from the corresponding saved 64-epoch PPP RINEX file above, adds the same
  native accumulated wind-up cycles to both raw carrier phases, then rounds
  phase fields again to 1e-4 cycles. Codes, LLI, strength, header/seed and
  event/time ordering remain byte-identical. This extra phase quantization
  explains small changes from the original truth errors. Existing SP3/CLK
  products and 36 Bias-SINEX OSBs are unchanged. No antenna, tide or physical
  yaw maneuver is injected. Native injection history covers all input rows;
  Rust commits only admitted phases (568 per trace), pruning G09 when masked.

Each entire trace outputs PPP FLOAT at all 64 epochs. The same truth-regression
bounds apply: noiseless maximum/final position <2 mm/1 mm, noisy <1 m/1 cm,
and final meter ambiguities <1 mm/1 cm respectively. Native true-geometry cycles
and IF additions match Rust posterior-geometry results within 1e-9 cycle and
1e-10 m noiseless, 1e-7 cycle and 1e-8 m noisy; these bounds explicitly include
the estimated receiver-coordinate difference. Final stored angles are also
checked against recomputation at the posterior receiver, same transmit
position and unchanged epoch cycle reference. Continuing arcs use the prior
accepted cycle count; new arcs evaluate the predicted geometry against zero
once and hold that candidate as their epoch reference. An analytic branch-cut
test and the PPP initial-anchor check verify this prevents relinearization
switching the integer near a half-cycle boundary. Candidates remain uncommitted
until the full update passes. Smooth wind-up updates preserve
every admitted arc; raw tracking identity and OSB calibration remain separate.

Additional PPP cases verify no premature cycle-cache commit during iterations
or rejected updates, duplicate-call immutability, slips, missing phase, sparse
events, power failure, external invalidation, and degenerate Sun-aligned
satellite attitude. Degenerate used phase models fail the epoch while numeric
state/covariance/time stay unchanged and continuity breaks. Rust rejects
missing/degenerate solar attitudes, unlike native's fallback/old-value return.
New arcs start with zero cycle reference; integer gauge changes are handled
by the newly initialized real IF ambiguity. There is no claim of native
whole-processor cache/yaw/initialization policy or real-data accuracy/runtime
parity. Receiver attitude estimation, block-specific yaw, eclipse/noon/night
maneuvers, antenna models and phase-model position derivatives remain absent.

## Absolute receiver ANTEX and PPP injection

`scripts/upstream_antenna_loader.cpp` includes the **actual pinned** `ppp.cpp`
and exposes `loadReceiverAntexOffsets` from its anonymous namespace. No native
source is edited. `scripts/upstream_antenna.cpp` calls this loader and the
unmodified `clasReceiverAntennaCorrectionMeters` from
`ppp_clas_osr_continuity.cpp`. PCV interpolation is the literal formula in
`PPPProcessor::receiverAntennaPcvMeters`; it is not an invocation of that private
processor method. Native load returns ENU; the CLAS helper accepts NEU, so the
generator explicitly swaps the first two components before that call.

The generated absolute ANTEX 1.4 contains a receiver `TESTANT NONE`, serial
`RX001`, G01/G02 offsets (12,-8,90)/(-5,18,125) mm and ten nonconstant NOAZI
nodes from zenith 0 to 90 degrees. A second satellite G01/G063 entry is retained
to verify receiver/satellite discrimination; its 2 m body offset is unused.
Validity labels are 2020-01-01 through 2030-01-01 on the GPS calendar, inclusive.
The strict Rust reader retains dates and serials that the native receiver
loader does not use in selection. Receiver delta is ENU (0.025,-0.035,0.8) m.

- `synthetic_receiver.atx`: complete independent calibration, including NOAZI
  rows extending beyond column 60.
- `upstream_receiver_antenna.csv`: 80 cases (2 frequencies, 5 azimuths, 8
  elevations including below horizon and above 90 degrees) from actual native
  offsets/range projection and the native interpolation formula. PCV tolerance
  is 1e-15 m; physically representable directions compare additive corrections
  within 3e-12 m. The >90-degree case checks only interpolation clamping.
- `upstream_ppp_receiver_antenna.csv`: 576 true-marker corrections (9 GPS,
  64 epochs at 30 seconds) using native precise transmit geometry, frequency
  corrections and IF combination.
- `synthetic_ppp_antenna.obs` / `synthetic_ppp_antenna_noisy.obs`: inherited
  wind-up-injected files with the native receiver range correction added to
  each code (rounded to 1 mm) and phase (rounded to 1e-4 cycles). SP3 remains APC,
  CLK/OSB/ambiguities/truth/noise/LLI and all headers are inherited. These are
  synthetic inputs, not real receiver calibration or measurements.

Rust adds `los·(delta+PCO)-PCV` to code/phase after OSB, separately from wind-up.
This is a first-order marker range correction. Native normal IF PPP shifts
receiver ECEF by IF-PCO and does not apply receiver PCV; this Rust IF-PCV path
is an extension, not whole-native-processor parity. The native CLAS helper is
the sign/axis component reference, not an emulated CLAS processing pipeline.
Model derivatives, exact geometry/Sagnac/troposphere at receiver APC, satellite
COM→APC, azimuth PCV, RMS, calibration switching and real-data performance are
not tested or implemented by this fixture.

Both complete inputs produce 64 PPP FLOAT epochs, 568 code and 568 phase rows,
9 satellites for the first 56 epochs and 8 thereafter. Continuous arcs are
retained despite changing projection/PCV. Maximum/final synthetic position
errors are 0.001902056/0.000066726 m without noise and
0.694594847/0.002670999 m with noise; final maximum ambiguity errors are
0.000056432/0.002987469 m. Epoch rejection on expiration or missing frequency
preserves numeric state and interrupts phase arcs; duplicate time changes none.

Reproduction (GCC 14.2.0 and pinned source/Eigen above):

```bash
g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core \
  -I/path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/algorithms -I/path/to/eigen \
  scripts/upstream_antenna.cpp scripts/upstream_antenna_loader.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/algorithms/ppp_clas_osr_continuity.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/types.cpp \
  /path/to/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/precise_products.cpp \
  -o /tmp/upstream-antenna
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-antenna-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-antenna /tmp/upstream-antenna-fixtures tests/fixtures
for file in synthetic_receiver.atx upstream_receiver_antenna.csv \
  upstream_ppp_receiver_antenna.csv synthetic_ppp_antenna.obs synthetic_ppp_antenna_noisy.obs; do
  cmp "tests/fixtures/$file" "/tmp/upstream-antenna-fixtures/$file" || exit 1
done
```

## Satellite ANTEX IF-PCO and COM→APC

`scripts/upstream_satellite_antenna.cpp` uses the **actual pinned** anonymous
`loadSatelliteAntexOffsets` through `scripts/upstream_antenna_loader.cpp`,
which includes unmodified `ppp.cpp`. It calls native IF coefficients,
precise transmit/clock/relativity/geodist, Niell, receiver antenna projection
and phase wind-up. The actual solar helper comes through
`scripts/upstream_windup_sun.cpp`, which includes unmodified
`ppp_corrections.cpp`. Satellite PCO rotation is the literal Eigen formula in
that file, not an invocation of the full private PPPProcessor path. It forms
the ECEF PCO before adding it once to COM, matching native operation order.

- `synthetic_satellite.atx`: nine GPS PRNs, fixed SVN G101/G102/G107/...,
  three frequencies G01/G02/G05, DAZI=0, eight zenith nodes 0–14 degrees,
  GPS validity 2020-01-01 through 2030-01-01 inclusive. All three body axes are
  nonzero. In mm, the frequency offsets for PRN p are (30p,-17p,2100+4p),
  (-22p,14p,2400+7p), (8p,31p,2200+5p). Nonzero satellite PCV is retained
  but unused, as in this native PCO path. The Rust binding requires SVN and
  freezes selection; native's first matching PRN/period policy is not copied.
- `synthetic_ppp_com.sp3`: the existing fictional orbit samples now explicitly
  declare COM. This is a synthetic product definition. It is **not** a method
  for converting a real APC SP3 by changing its comment. Existing CLK values
  are bound by the generator to the newly declared synthetic clock/PCO model.
- `upstream_satellite_antenna.csv`: 81 cases, nine PRNs × epochs 0/31/63 ×
  L1/L2, reversed L2/L1, L1/L5. Actual loaded offsets/IF coefficient/Sun,
  independent native nominal-yaw rotation, APC/range/elevation/Niell/code
  prediction/design and unchanged COM-based corrected clock. Body IF tolerance
  2e-14 m, ECEF offset 2e-12 m, COM/APC/range/prediction 1e-6 m,
  elevation 1e-11 rad, Niell/design 1e-10, clock 1e-16 s.
- `upstream_ppp_satellite_antenna.csv`: 576 truth rows, nine PRNs × 64 epochs,
  true APC/geometry/wind-up/receiver IF correction and elevation admission.
- `synthetic_ppp_satellite_antenna.obs` and `_noisy.obs`: complete independent
  native formula including COM→APC, receiver delta/PCO/NOAZI and native phase
  wind-up. Headers/time/LLI and known bias/ambiguity/iono/noise formula come
  from the previous PPP generator. All code and phase values are recomputed
  before **one** final RINEX rounding (1e-5 m code, 1e-4 cycles phase), rather
  than adding corrections to already rounded carrier counters. Both frequency
  rows use the native IF APC range, as in the normal IF observation model.

The satellite body convention is x/north-of-antenna, y/east-of-antenna,
z/boresight toward Earth. It is not the receiver's NEU→ENU permutation.
Attitude uses COM and the approximate Sun at GPS reception time. APC geometry,
Sagnac, elevation/Niell/design, receiver correction and wind-up are recomputed
after the shift; transmit time, velocity, clock and relativity remain those of
COM. No observation-level satellite PCO is additionally applied. No satellite
PCV, actual/eclipsed yaw, EOP/UT1 or PCO/attitude receiver derivative is included.

Rust admits PCO only for COM input and requires it there. APC input rejects
the model to prevent double application. Selected PRN/SVN/calibration and
tracking pair remain fixed for the filter lifetime. ANTEX compatibility with
clock datum is an explicit caller assertion; it is not inferred from headers.
PPP checks selected signals/datum/source and the actual CLK/SP3 source.
Missing/expired calibration or degenerate attitude rejects the entire numeric
update and interrupts phase continuity, rather than admitting uncorrected COM.

Both complete inputs produce all 64 epochs as PPP FLOAT with 568 code/phase
rows each, continuous arcs and matching admission (nine satellites for 56
epochs, eight for the final eight). Maximum/final synthetic position errors are
0.001782562/0.000020278 m without noise, 0.696218866/0.002610997 m with noise;
final maximum ambiguity errors are 0.000011506/0.003010892 m. Six new PPP tests
cover final-geometry/phase consistency, unchanged clock, COM/APC misuse,
datum/source mismatch, missing/expired calibration, duplicate preservation and
degenerate attitude even with wind-up disabled. Four new component tests cover
axes/pairs, selection/period/ambiguity, binding/frequency and attitude failures.
These are component comparisons and synthetic truth results, not native whole
processor, real ANTEX/clock compatibility or real-data accuracy/runtime parity.

## Legacy Love-number solid Earth tide and instantaneous PPP receiver

`scripts/upstream_tides.cpp` calls the **actual pinned** anonymous
`approximateMoonPositionECEF`, `approximateSunPositionECEF`, and
`bodyTideDisplacement` from `ppp_corrections.cpp` through the compiled bridge
`scripts/upstream_windup_sun.cpp`. The upstream file itself is unchanged.
The native normal PPP default is `use_iers_solid_tide=true` (IERS 2010
Step-1+2); these fixtures explicitly cover its **false/legacy alternative**,
not IERS or the native processor's default output.

The native legacy displacement uses fixed degree-2 h2=.6078 and l2=.0847,
Earth GM=3.986004418e14, Sun GM=1.32712440018e20, Moon GM=4.902801e12,
WGS84 equatorial radius, **geodetic** up and geocentric body direction.
Each body's scale is `(GM_body/GM_earth)*(a/distance)^3*a`, with radial
`h2*(1.5*cosine^2-.5)*up` and tangential
`3*l2*cosine*(body_unit-cosine*up)` terms. The sum is **added once** to
nominal marker coordinates. The low-order Sun/Moon and GMST use the same
fractional GPS-labelled calendar as native helpers, without leap-second,
UT1, polar-motion or high-accuracy celestial ephemeris corrections.
No permanent-tide convention transformation, ocean loading, pole tide or
atmospheric loading is represented.

Eight generated files are retained:

- `upstream_legacy_moon.csv`: 12 actual native Moon vectors, weeks
  0/1042/2300/2301 and TOW 0/346200.25/604799.75. Absolute tolerance 1e-6 m.
- `upstream_legacy_solid_tide.csv`: 252 actual body-helper cases at those
  times, seven latitudes −90/−60/−35/0/35/60/90 degrees, three longitudes
  −170/0/139 degrees, cycling heights −50/45/1500 m. Individual Sun/Moon
  and total displacement tolerance 2e-12 m; instantaneous XYZ 1e-8 m.
- `upstream_ppp_legacy_tide_model.csv`: 54 full geometry cases, nine PRNs,
  epochs 0/31/63 and true/offset (+5,−3,+2 m) nominal receivers. Tide is
  applied **before** precise transmit time. Native precise components,
  satellite IF-PCO rotation, Niell and literal PPP expressions are reused
  from the previous independent generators. Receiver/COM/APC XYZ, range
  and code prediction tolerate 1e-6 m; elevation 1e-11 rad; mapping/design
  1e-10; clock 1e-16 s; light-time 1e-13 s. These are not calls to a complete
  native PPP filter; satellite rotation/design expressions have the same
  qualifications as the previous section.
- `upstream_ppp_legacy_tide.csv`: 576 truth wind-up cycles, receiver IF
  additions and elevation-admission decisions (nine SVs for epochs 0–55,
  eight for 56–63). All geometry and receiver corrections use the
  instantaneous receiver, including the native wind-up's continuous branch.
- `synthetic_ppp_legacy_tide_truth.csv`: all 64 nominal marker XYZ, tide
  displacement XYZ and instantaneous marker XYZ. Nominal receiver is
  latitude 35°, longitude 139°, height 45 m; GPS week 2300/TOW 346200,
  spaced 30 s. First displacement norm is 0.092868147 m.
- `synthetic_ppp_legacy_tide.obs` and `_noisy.obs`: complete independent
  raw code/carrier recomputations with all previous OSB, receiver antenna,
  satellite PCO and wind-up terms, plus instantaneous receiver geometry.
  Previous PPP observations supply only RINEX headers/epochs/field layout;
  values are not adjusted from already-rounded carriers. Each raw value is
  rounded once (code 1e-5 m, phase 1e-4 cycles). The previous COM SP3, CLK,
  absolute receiver/satellite ANTEX and Bias-SINEX products are reused.
  Clock is `2e-6 + epoch*5e-10` seconds; ZTD 2.4 m. Noise retains previous
  deterministic 5 cm code and 1 mm carrier amplitude conventions.
- `upstream_ppp_legacy_tide_unrounded.csv`: 576 rows of the corresponding
  noiseless C++ code/carrier values at 17-digit precision before RINEX
  rounding, for an independent input-precision control.

Both rounded inputs produce all 64 PPP FLOAT epochs, each with 568 code
and 568 phase rows, matching admission and continuous arcs. Maximum/final
3D errors are 0.003571701/0.000011410 m noiseless and
0.696207136/0.002606282 m noisy. Final maximum IF-ambiguity errors are
0.000014313/0.003002153 m; phase RMS 0.000008792/0.001214300 m.
These are **synthetic truth regressions**, not native full-solver or measured
accuracy comparisons. The rounded noiseless regression uses a 5 mm maximum
and 1 mm final bound; noisy maximum/final bounds are 1 m/1 cm. The component
comparison tolerances above remain independent of these truth bounds.

The unrounded control preserves the same model, prior, noise settings and
all 64 epochs; only input quantization changes. Maximum/final error is
0.000416336/0.000000109 m (bounds 0.5 mm/1 µm). Rounded raw phase differs by
at most 0.000049964 cycles, within the declared half-unit; code differences
are checked against 5.01e-6 m. The initial height/ZTD transient amplifies
carrier quantization, with the rounded maximum at epoch 1. These two
precision levels are kept separate; the 5 mm bound is not a native solver
parity tolerance. No epochs are removed from the reported maxima.

Additional cases check radial/tangential signs, inverse-cube body-distance
scaling, geodetic up, week-rollover continuity, zero/nonfinite bodies, invalid
station/GM/calendar, reference/model contradictions, and one-time correction
application. Rust returns explicit errors where native legacy helpers may
return zero. PPP rejection preserves numeric state/time and interrupts arcs
and wind-up; duplicate input leaves them unchanged. Disabled tide on the
first epoch recovers the instantaneous marker and differs by over 8 cm
from the nominal marker, rather than being compared as the same datum.
NominalMarker declares only a coordinate before this selected model; it
does not assert a standard tide-free/zero-tide terrestrial reference.
Receiver tide derivatives are omitted like mapping/orbit derivatives in
the initial solver. Real-data accuracy, native IERS and native PPPProcessor
state/covariance/continuity/runtime parity remain untested or unimplemented.

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-tide-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-tides /tmp/upstream-tide-fixtures tests/fixtures
for file in upstream_legacy_moon.csv upstream_legacy_solid_tide.csv \
```

## IERS 2010 Dehant Step-1+2 explicit-body component

`scripts/upstream_iers2010.cpp` compiles the **actual unchanged** pinned
`third_party/ginan-iers2010/dehanttideinel/dehanttide_all.cpp` and calls
`iers2010::dehanttideinel_impl`. Including this translation unit exposes its
actual `st1idiu`, `st1isem`, `st1l1`, `step2diu`, `step2lon` and angle/site
helpers for term-by-term comparison. The degree-2/3 fixture term is the
native total minus those native correction terms; it is not recomputed
using Rust expressions. The implementation's SHA-256 is
`973dca9acab3b459bef996cb45f18b0c84829b25def56068da2ba20c8d639bce`.

The Rust translation is `src/iers2010.rs`, licensed Apache 2.0 under
`LICENSE-IERS2010` with Geoscience Australia/Ginan/IERS attribution and
modifications recorded in `NOTICE-IERS2010`. The upstream Apache text is
retained byte-identically. No SOFA source, foreign-function binding or Rust
dependency is included in the Rust implementation. The fixture generator
alone links the unchanged pinned SOFA 2021-05-12 C library.

- `upstream_iers2010_kernel.csv`: 505 cases. Row 0 is the published
  DEHANTTIDEINEL reference station/Sun/Moon at 2009-04-13 00:00 UTC,
  MJD 54934, TT−UTC=66.184 seconds. Published expected displacement is
  `(0.07700420357108126, 0.06304056321824968, 0.05516568152597247)` m;
  the published-reference tolerance is 1e-6 m. Another 504 cases cross
  TT centuries −.5/−.2/0/.0928/.24/.5, UT hours 0/6.25/12.5/23.999999,
  latitudes −89.999/−60/−35/0/35/60/89.999 degrees, longitudes −170/0/139
  degrees and cycling heights −50/45/1500 m. The reference Sun/Moon
  vectors are rotated about the terrestrial z axis by `UT_hour*15 + t*37`
  degrees to exercise geometry; those 504 inputs are **component test
  vectors**, not astronomical ephemerides at the nominal TT epochs.
  Rows retain nominal XYZ, both body vectors, all six components, total
  displacement and instantaneous XYZ. Each component and total is
  compared at absolute 2e-12 m; instantaneous XYZ at 1e-8 m.
- `upstream_iers2010_epochs.csv`: 150 inputs from the **actual native**
  `solidEarthTideDisplacementAt`, `sunPositionIcrs`, `moonPositionIcrs`
  and `icrsToItrs`, compiled with SOFA. Start MJD UTC 54934/60348/60908,
  each with 25 hourly epochs including the following midnight. Two
  EOP settings are zero and synthetic nonzero UT1−UTC=−.1234 s,
  xp=.1 arcsec, yp=−.2 arcsec. Station latitude alternates +35/−35
  degrees, longitude 139°, height 45 m. The fixture retains UTC MJD,
  SOFA-derived TT centuries, the wrapper's fractional UTC hour used
  as UT, EOP values and **already rotated ITRS** Sun/Moon vectors.
  Rust consumes those explicit bodies/time arguments; the total
  native wrapper displacement matches within 2e-12 m, instantaneous
  XYZ within 1e-8 m. This verifies the kernel on native astronomical
  inputs, **not** a Rust implementation of SOFA, UTC/TT conversion,
  EOP evaluation or ICRS→ITRS rotation.

The kernel uses geocentric station latitude and the IERS radius
6378136.6 m, not the legacy geodetic-up/WGS84 expression. Latitude-dependent
Love numbers, degree 3, mantle anelasticity, latitude dependence and
31 diurnal/5 long-period frequency terms are retained. Permanent-tide
Step-3 remains omitted exactly as in the upstream kernel. It does not
establish a tide-free/zero-tide datum transformation.

Seven tests also verify TT/UT dependence, UT-midnight continuity, a
nontrivial difference from the legacy Love-number model, input/result
finiteness, body norms, invalid UT hours, invalid stations and undefined
longitude on the exact terrestrial axis. Rust rejects exact-axis station
inputs with `AxialStation`, rather than native division by zero; near-pole
cases remain in the numerical comparison. `EarthFixedSunMoon` is an
explicit caller contract for frame, metres and epoch. Vector magnitude
cannot prove a celestial-to-terrestrial rotation. `IersTideArguments`
accepts TT centuries and UT hours, not GPS TOW or UTC MJD directly.

This component does not change `PppConfig.solid_earth_tide`: that path
still supports the legacy approximation only. Automatic Rust ephemerides,
time-scale conversion, Earth rotation/EOP and the complete IERS PPP path
remain pending. These files do not compare native PPP state, covariance,
continuity, real-data accuracy, runtime or memory.

Reproduction (g++/gcc 14.2.0, pinned Eigen 3.4.0 as above) builds the
247 intact SOFA C sources excluding its self-test entry point. The build
is local to `/tmp` and needs no downloaded dependencies or CMake:

```bash
set -e
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
root = Path('/workspace/.cloud-setup/reference/gnssplusplus-library/third_party/sofa/src')
build = Path('/tmp/gnss-rust-sofa-reference')
```

## GPS-era time scales, ERA, polar motion and supplied-CIO composition

`scripts/upstream_earth_rotation.cpp` links the pinned native
`src/iers/earth_rotation.cpp` and the unchanged SOFA 2021-05-12 reference
library built above. `upstream_earth_rotation.csv` contains 558 rows:
six GPS weeks (0/1042/1527/1930/2300/2380), four fractional TOWs
(0/1.125/346200.25/604799.75), three synthetic EOP settings, and 18 known
leap transitions × nine relative epochs × the same three EOPs.
The epochs relative to effective GPS midnight are −86400.25/−43200.25/
−20/−1.25/−.75/−.25/0/.25/20 seconds, including UTC insertion instants.
EOP settings are (DUT1 seconds, xp arcsec, yp arcsec)
`(0,0,0)`, `(−.1234,.1,−.2)`, `(.3345,.2,−.4)`; they are test values,
not observed EOP or physical continuity series.

The oracle forms precise day/second TAI from GPS +19 s and uses actual
`iauTaiutc`, `iauD2dtf`, `iauDat`, `iauTaitt`, `iauUtcut1`, `iauEra00`,
`iauSp00`, `iauPom00`, `iauC2i06a`, `iauC2tcio`. It retains UTC day,
physical seconds/day length/TAI−UTC, quasi-MJD, TT/UT1 day and seconds,
ERA, s′, and the celestial→intermediate, polar and composed matrices.
Rust supplies no SOFA source or FFI and does not generate precession-nutation;
the celestial→intermediate matrix is supplied from the fixture.
Time seconds compare at absolute 3e-9 s, quasi-MJD at 1e-11 day,
ERA/matrices at 2e-12, TT centuries at 1e-16 and UTC approximate UT hour
at 1e-12 hour. Frame, epoch and model of the supplied CIO matrix are
caller contracts in addition to numeric proper-rotation validation.

The native one-pass `gnssTimeToMjdUtc` result is retained separately.
It uses an approximate GPS-labelled date to choose the leap offset and
returns days divided by 86400, whereas SOFA UTC quasi-MJD divides leap
days by 86401. On non-leap days the results agree within 1e-11 day.
On leap days 330 rows differ by over 1 µs (MJD difference ×86400),
with maximum 0.999985775 s. The test investigates and preserves this
known policy difference; it does not widen tolerances or call that native
wrapper correct at those boundaries. Rust follows the direct SOFA
GPS→TAI→UTC reference. No native full-processor parity is implied.

Six tests check every reference row, leap-second labels, half-open table
coverage, explicit synthetic future updates, invalid/negative/duplicate
leap series, nonfinite inputs, numeric overflow, invalid proper rotations,
inverse/direction/arcsecond units and fractional week rollover.
A separate leap-continuity case supplies the physical DUT1 jump from
−.4 to +.6 seconds across midnight and checks uniform TT/UT1 and ERA
continuity. The leap table's product name and validity end are explicit;
the test uses a frozen through-2017 table and a caller-declared exclusive
end MJD 61000 for these fixture dates. This does not attest to current
announcements. Pre-GPS epochs and negative leap seconds are unsupported.
The shared historical dates keep existing RINEX UTC conversion policy.

```bash
set -e
g++ -std=c++20 -O1 -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Wl,--gc-sections \
  -I/workspace/.cloud-setup/reference/gnssplusplus-library/include \
  -I/workspace/.cloud-setup/reference/gnssplusplus-library/third_party/sofa/src \
  -I/tmp/gnss-rust-eigen-3.4.0 scripts/upstream_earth_rotation.cpp \
  /workspace/.cloud-setup/reference/gnssplusplus-library/src/iers/earth_rotation.cpp \
  /workspace/.cloud-setup/reference/gnssplusplus-library/src/core/types.cpp \
  /tmp/gnss-rust-sofa-reference/libsofa.a -o /tmp/upstream-earth-rotation
mkdir -p /tmp/upstream-earth-rotation-fixtures
/tmp/upstream-earth-rotation /tmp/upstream-earth-rotation-fixtures
cmp tests/fixtures/upstream_earth_rotation.csv \
  /tmp/upstream-earth-rotation-fixtures/upstream_earth_rotation.csv
```
